hypothesis: Newly critical connections may retain a path selected at lower criticality because ordinary pending nets are driven by failure/overuse. A bounded supplemental net requeue may improve timing; no benefit or stopping bug is assumed.
selection_rule: After each actual STA update, identify nets with any connection crossing from below the existing criticality cap64880 to at/above it. Add a net only if ordinary next-pending does not already contain it and it has not previously received a supplemental requeue in this run. Apply uniformly to all nets; task934 is motivation, not a selection condition.
budget_rule: Keep max30 routing iterations. At most one supplemental requeue per net; only consume that allowance for an actual additional scheduled net. At the iteration limit preserve a legal converged route and log unserved feedback rather than reporting a timing-refinement failure as loss of routing legality.
fixed: same core/source/runner for control and candidate
native indexed costs and timing updates
required_component_checks: New critical net is additionally rerouted and uses fresh criticality
Already-pending net does not consume supplemental allowance
Once-per-net bound across repeated cap crossings
Legal route retained when no iteration budget remains
Reject enabling feedback without a timing analyzer
No effects on another net ownership/version state
required_workload_evidence: Five repetitions per configuration with deterministic traces
Record raw cap-crossing events, ordinary/supplemental pending decisions and budget skips
acceptance: Existing G4 joint baseline gates remain unchanged; do not adopt on a single improved metric or this development case alone.
scope: CPU algorithmic ablation for quality diagnosis, not a new DieRoute architecture or hardware result. Heldout designs remain unopened.
